title: Connection URL for DroneCore applications
body:
As DroneCore supports multiple connection interfaces TCP, UDP & Serial, we need to allow user to select either of them while launching the application.
Examples of connection URL could be:

- UDP: `udp://[bind_host][:port]`
- TCP client: `tcp://[server_host][:port]`
- Serial: `/path/to/serial/device[:baudrate]`

For.eg below conn URL _binds to UDP port 14500_
```
$ ./takeoff_land udp://:14500
```
binds to default UDP port 14540
```
$ ./takeoff_land
```
Connects to TCP Server (`192.168.8.2:5760`) hosted by MAVLink Router on Intel Aero
```
$ ./takeoff_land tcp://192.168.8.2:5760
```
etc.

title: Migration to MAVLink organisation
body:
Copying @hamishwillee's message on the PX4 Slack, to keep a record of the discussion.

The MAVLink dev team accepted the "MAVLink RFC Proposal" so we'll be taking the Dronecode SDK into the MAVLink organisation and renaming it to the "MAVSDK": https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/blob/master/text/0011-mavlink-sdk.md

### Code


* [x] Agree on new names for SDK repos
 => Will be `MAVSDK`, `MAVSDK-Proto`, `MAVSDK-Swift`, `MAVSDK-Python`, etc.
* [x] Move all SDK repos into github mavlink org
* [x] Agree new names for namespaces and other code items
 => The documentation and official name is `MAVSDK`, but the code doesn't have to follow that. We will generally prefer lowercase (i.e. namespace: `mavsdk::`), and we may capitalize if necessary (e.g. `class MavSdk`).
* [x] Update code in line with new names
* [ ] Update READMEs with appropriate new links to repos and docs
* [x] Make an official first release. Would this be 1.0?
 => The release will not be 1.0, but just the continuation of current releases, each repo going at its own speed. The Python SDK will be released as `0.1.0` on pip ASAP.
* [x] Make sure all old repositories redirect correctly

### Docs


* [x] Design of new logo & tagline
 => Taken care of in #750.
* [x] Confirm name of docs repo in mavlink org [I think `sdk_docs` to `mavsdk_docs`]
* [x] Move docs repo into mavlink org
* [x] Update head revision docs API reference
* [x] Update docs guide materials
* [ ] Review/update docs on marketing/positioning. Ie where it is hosted and the goals.
* [x] Decide what to do about previous releases/docs. These all will refer to the Dronecode SDK.
* [x] Propose that we delete all the old ones and start from scratch with a master release and initial release
* [x] Re-sync via gitbook
* [x] Get new domain/URL. 
 Current: `https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/`. Proposed: `https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/en/`. This is probably easier than try to do `mavlink.io/mavlink`, `mavlink.io/mavsdk` etc.
* [x] Themes updates
 The theme for the SDK becomes more like the mavlink.io one: https://mavlink.io/en/
* [x] Other dronecode sites will need to have theme updated to point to SDK and any notes about SDK updated too.
* [x] Make sure all old docs links redirect correctly

### Dronecode Website


* [ ] Update top bar
 This is likely to be SLOW process.
* [x] Update SDK page and other mentions.

### Channels


* [x] Discussion board category rename
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)
  * [x] Update category post link to URL when SDK URL moves: https://discuss.px4.io/t/about-the-mavsdk-category/4234
* [x] Slack channel rename to `#mavsdk`
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)

title: Generalizing MAVSDK for non-autopilot control
body:
Traditionally, MAVSDK has been used to connect solely to a drone in order to control it; connecting to other peripherals has been more of an addon than a main feature. While this is definitely the main use case of MAVSDK, I think it would be nice to be able to use MAVSDK as a more generic high level platform for any MAVLink communication. This would increase the number of use cases and platforms MAVSDK can be deployed to, and also allow some very interesting new possibilities. Below are some comments on what the current state of affairs is and what can be done to improve this without sacrificing ease-of-use.

The base `Mavsdk` class define the source system and component, which defines the local side of the communication. With the recent addition of the `Configuration` class, this is fine - the system and component ID can be changed without restrictions, and there are sane defaults. From here on, though, things get a bit more complicated.

The `System` class, although designed to connect to any MAVLink compatible system, is in reality only tailored to connect to a single autopilot. This causes problems, obviously, when connecting to anything *other* than the autopilot. Peripherals such as gimbals and cameras are supported; however, they are all connected to the parent `System` rather than a parent `Mavsdk`, which makes more sense to me. As a result, you need to connect to an autopilot before getting access to any peripherals. Additionally, although MAVSDK can be used to control an autopilot from a companion computer, how MAVSDK handles connecting to a different component on the same system is uncertain and definitely undocumented.

To be completely honest, from looking into the core source code, I feel the code to handle system and component ids is very messy; a good portion of it is probably very old code, but I think we can do better. For example, there is a lot of hard-coding "let's throw away messages from these ids", "lets assume this component ID means this", etc. This leaves very little room for anything that deviates from the standard "I have a ground station which connects to my drone, both with standard IDs." I'd like to be able to use MAVSDK for more complex things including intra-system (inter-component) communication. I'm happy to take charge of cleaning some of it up + documenting it, if we can agree on what to do! For starters, I think we should all read https://mavlink.io/en/guide/routing.html :smile: 

I'm not sure the best way to do this, since I don't want to break the current API (create a System from a Mavsdk, create plugins from the System). One idea I had was to create a `Component` or similar, which is a more high level representation of a target that MAVSDK can connect to. The `Mavsdk` class can then search for and connect to multiple `Components`, and the existing `System` would be a type of `Component` (not sure if System is even the right word for it, in that sense, but I'm hesitant to break the current API). O
...[truncated]

title: SIGABRT when destructing mavsdk
body:
In order to start fresh after detecting a disconnect (we want to reconnect on a potentially different IP address), we have to destruct the mavsdk object and create a brand new one. However, I have seen 2 exceptions come up when destructing the mavsdk.

I have attached a CMakeLists.txt and relevant minimal examples. Change the source `.txt` files to `.cpp`. Here is the CMake line:
`cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=install -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug ..`

It is also worth noting that I am connecting to the simulator using a remote port and UDP. Usage is similar to `mavsdk_server`:
`case1 udp://<url>:14540`. I am also using a REQUIRED code change from [this PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2074) to allow the UDP disconnect to be properly recognized.

1. When registering on the `subscribe_is_connected` and then killing the simulator after a successful connection, I get a SIGABRT on [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ea0b720538cff8e51947557234cb9c4300edadc3/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L53). I made sure to unsubscribe from all subscriptions before destructing the mavsdk, but it still seems to be holding onto something. The error on screen is `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: thread::join failed: Resource deadlock avoided`. I have attached this as case1.cpp. This code gives you 120 seconds to kill the simulator and detect the failure.
2. After the mavsdk is destructed, it looks like the system_thread is still running, but the `_parent.time` has been uninitialized and leads to a `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x10)` exception on [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ea0b720538cff8e51947557234cb9c4300edadc3/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_time.cpp#L45).

[CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/11702438/CMakeLists.txt)
[case2.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/11702441/case2.txt)
[case1.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/11702442/case1.txt)

Initial discussion conducted on [discord](https://discord.com/channels/1022170275984457759/1116075629008392314)

I am using [my PR branch](https://github.com/jperez-droneup/MAVSDK/tree/UDP-heartbeat-disconnect), which is based off of today's trunk `MAVSDK version: v1.4.0-484-gc1006bf3`. I was using a slightly older version previously, it looks like case2 has been fixed since then. However case1 is still present.

1. Oh, I see the problem. You are trying to destruct the `Mavsdk` instance while you are inside the callback. That can't really work. I took the inspiration from your case1 and created an example: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2078 Let me know if that could work for you.

2. This one runs fine for me. Maybe it has been fixed recently on `main`?

Indeed this was a user error - I didn't realize that the thread being joined was the thread causing the destruction. But yes, having a way to remove the connection without having to destruct the mavsdk at all is definitely better. Thanks for your fast responses!

title: set_rate_attitude(): ignores requested rate
body:
Hi,
Working with SITL, I see that as the SITL starts working it sends various messages at given rates.
For example the attitude message is sent every 250ms.

When I run:
telemetry.set_rate_attitude(1.0);

It does not have any affect on the message rate.
So is true for other "set rates".

What do I need to do to overcome this?
Thanks

comments.body: Is this PX4?
arducopter

> telemetry.set_rate_attitude(1.0);

1/4=0.25=250ms, does 1 = 250ms?

The [example code](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/tree/main/examples) does not have [set rate calling for battery, after code change for my case it works with Pi4B](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/issues/453#issuecomment-1790270693). I have not verified whether the sending speed changes with different values.

I tried to change it to `await drone.telemetry.set_rate_battery(2) #2hz`, the number of printouts is the same which is controlled by these lines `await asyncio.sleep(3)
    telem_battery.cancel()`. the printouts did not double as what I had expected.

Not sure of [anything to do with this parameter](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/battery-status-not-updating-at-desired-frequency/92841/1).

[This may interest us](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-telemetry-port-setup.html#mavlink1-mavlink2-and-stream-rates).

After changing this at the Arducopter side [SRx_EXTRA3,2 (500 msec)](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/parameters.html#sr1-extra3-extra-data-type-3-stream-rate), regardless of `drone.telemetry.set_rate_battery(x)` value set, the printouts are doubled. previously was six (3+3) printouts, now I have twelve (6+6).

Most ground stations set the desired stream rate by sending the [REQUEST_DATA_STREAM MAVLink message](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/mavlink-requesting-data.html#mavlink-requesting-data) to the vehicle instead of directly setting the parameters ment
